items.stem: You are implementing a Figma screen that uses the team's design system. What is the most durable way to apply colour and spacing?

options.text: Map the design's tokens to the design-system token variables and use those
options.rationale: Correct: using shared tokens keeps the UI consistent and maintainable.

options.text: Copy the raw hex and pixel values from the mock into each component
options.rationale: Hard-coded values drift from the system and are hard to maintain.

options.text: Eyeball the colours from a screenshot
options.rationale: Eyeballing is inaccurate and ignores the token source of truth.

options.text: Let the AI tool invent its own palette

items.explanation: Correct: using shared tokens keeps the UI consistent and maintainable.

items.stem: An AI tool generated a UI from a Figma frame. Which TWO checks should you always run before accepting it? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Verify the markup is semantic and accessible (landmarks, labels, contrast)
options.rationale: Correct: generated markup is often not accessible by default and must be checked.

options.text: Confirm it uses design-system components and tokens rather than ad-hoc styles
options.rationale: Correct: consistency with the system is a core acceptance criterion.

options.text: Check that the file has a high number of code comments
options.rationale: Comment count is not an acceptance criterion for UI fidelity or accessibility.

options.text: Confirm the tool used the largest available model
options.rationale: Model size does not determine whether the output meets the design and accessibility bar.

items.explanation: Correct: generated markup is often not accessible by default and must be checked.

items.stem: A generated screen looks right on desktop but the designer reports issues. What should you check first?

options.text: Responsive behaviour and component states at the other breakpoints and states
options.rationale: Correct: fidelity gaps often appear in untested breakpoints and states.

options.text: Whether the Figma file has enough viewers
options.rationale: File popularity is irrelevant to implementation fidelity.

options.text: Whether to switch to a different programming language
options.rationale: Language choice does not address responsive fidelity.

options.text: Whether to delete the design tokens
options.rationale: Removing tokens would worsen consistency, not fix the gap.

items.explanation: Correct: fidelity gaps often appear in untested breakpoints and states.
